outcomes.description: Configure and persist OIDC session credentials used to authenticate automated Playwright test runs against the target application.

scenarios.scenario: Persist OIDC session credentials to the test runner global configuration
scenarios.description: Admin supplies an OIDC session key and value (JSON) captured from a browser session, optionally masks the value for on-screen privacy, and saves the credentials into global-setup.js on the server so subsequent automated test runs can reuse them without re-entry. Saving creates a timestamped backup of the existing configuration file before overwriting it.

actions.action: Show or hide the authentication section
actions.description: Show/Hide control in the Authentication header toggles visibility of the OIDC Key/Value inputs within the Test Configuration panel; type: boolean display state; default: visible (true).

actions.action: Set masked display of the OIDC value
actions.description: label: Mask OIDC value; type: boolean; required: false; default: false; when enabled, the OIDC Value textarea displays 8 masked bullet characters instead of the raw JSON and becomes read-only; disabled when the authentication section is hidden.
Reveal control is shown only when masked display is enabled; activating it sets masked display back to false so the raw OIDC Value JSON is shown again.

label: OIDC Key; type: text; required: true to save; default: empty string; placeholder: oidc.user:...; disabled while a test run is in progress or while the authentication section is hidden; help text explains the value is the session-storage key found via browser DevTools, Application, Session.

label: OIDC Value (JSON); type: JSON text (multiline); required: true to save; default: empty string; placeholder: an id_token JSON blob; validation: must parse as valid JSON (client-side JSON.parse) both before running a test and before saving; invalid JSON blocks the save and shows an error notification asking to fix the JSON before saving; disabled while a test run is in progress, the authentication section is hidden, or masked display is enabled; help text explains the value is the session-storage value copied from browser DevTools, Application, Session.

steps.step: Submit the OIDC credentials for persistence

actions.action: Submit OIDC credentials to server configuration
actions.description: Requires both OIDC Key and OIDC Value to be non-empty, otherwise blocked client-side with a notification to provide both before saving; requires the user to confirm a security warning that this will write sensitive OIDC data into global-setup.js on the server as a permanent file change before sending; on the server, a timestamped backup of global-setup.js is created (global-setup.js.bak.timestamp) before the defaultOidcKey and defaultOidcValue constants in that file are rewritten with the submitted values.

apis.request: JSON body: oidcKey (string), oidcValue (object, parsed OIDC JSON)
apis.response: 200: success true and a backup file path; 400: missing oidcKey or oidcValue, or OIDC value is not valid JSON; 500: global-setup.js not found on server, or an exception message

warnings.note: The Code_Graph_Search tool was not present in this session's tool list (only Read, Glob, Grep, Bash were available). Discovery was completed via exhaustive Read, Glob, Grep instead: App.jsx is the entire frontend (main.jsx only bootstraps it, styles.css is pure CSS), and server.js and global-setup.js were read in full to resolve every fetch call and the save-oidc file-persistence logic. Grep sweeps for role, permission, admin, persona patterns across the frontend and server.js returned zero hits.

No role, permission, feature-flag, or subscription-tier conditional rendering exists anywhere in App.jsx or server.js; every control on the dashboard is visible identically regardless of persona. Per the EXISTING_NEIGHBORHOOD note, the run, monitor, stop, reset, report scenarios are already captured under the QA Engineer persona; this Admin payload is scoped to the config-persistence (save OIDC to file) capability that the QA Engineer payload explicitly deferred to Admin, rather than re-declaring identical shared dashboard actions.
